text: According to the coherence theory of truth, a belief is true if and only if:
choices: it corresponds to an independently existing fact or state of affairs in a mind-independent world
it coheres with a sufficiently comprehensive, mutually supporting, and consistent system of beliefs
acting on it reliably leads to successful outcomes and satisfies our cognitive needs
the equivalence schema '“snow is white” is true iff snow is white' holds for it, and nothing more need be said
explanation: The coherence theory, rooted in British Idealism (Bradley, Bosanquet), makes truth a matter of a belief's fitting harmoniously into a maximally coherent system rather than of matching an external fact. Option 0 states the rival correspondence theory; option 2 states James's pragmatist 'what works' account; option 3 states deflationism. Coherence here means more than bare consistency: mutual support and explanatory connectedness as well.
